nodes.label: Dispatch Engine (System Actor)
nodes.rationale: Modelled as a separate non-human actor rather than as internal system behaviour, indicating automated technician matching and job-offer creation is intended as an autonomous service independent of the admin and of client action.

nodes.label: Submit Service Request
nodes.rationale: Central client use case: it is the hub that Cancel Service Request and Track Assigned Technician include, and it includes Identify Eligible Technicians, so submitting a request is what triggers automated dispatch.

nodes.label: Complete Service
nodes.rationale: Rate & Review Service includes Complete Service, so a review can only exist for a job the technician has marked complete - this prevents ratings on unfinished work.

nodes.label: Validate Technician
nodes.rationale: Validation includes reviewing verification documents, making manual admin approval a gate between technician signup and eligibility for dispatch - a trust/quality control on the marketplace supply side.

nodes.label: Rank by Active Jobs
nodes.rationale: Ranking candidates by current active job count is a deliberate load-balancing / fairness heuristic: work is spread to the least-busy eligible technician rather than assigned first-come or by rating alone.

nodes.label: Create Job Offer
nodes.rationale: Dispatch produces an offer the technician can accept or reject rather than a forced assignment, preserving technician autonomy and implying a fallback to the next-ranked candidate.

nodes.label: Automated Dispatch Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Request -> eligibility filter -> rank by active jobs -> job offer is modelled as a chain of «include» use cases owned by a machine actor, so matching is automated and rule-based, with no admin in the assignment loop.
